original: 二九日 一五一五 N一七-一三 E一一八-二二 みりい丸 さらわく丸 (小破)
translation: 29th, 1515, N 17°13′ E 118°22′: Miri Maru and Sarawak Maru (minor damage)
note: 1st Surface Escort Division war diary, June 1944, chart 別表第二 船団護衛状況(馬来直航路) (convoy escort, Malay direct route): handwritten beside a torpedo symbol on convoy ヒ67 (HI-67)'s track, which ends at (マニラ) Manila. Written in Arabic numerals in the original (290 1515 / N17-13 / E118-22)

original: (ハ) 小破 有馬山丸、神州丸、みりい丸、さらわく丸、まりふ丸 中破 能登呂
translation: (c) Minor damage: Arimasan Maru, Shinshu Maru, Miri Maru, Sarawak Maru, Marifu Maru. Moderate damage: Notoro
note: Same diary, notes to table 別表第一 (escort statistics, June). Neither oiler is in the June list of ships sunk by submarine (9 ships, 43,073 tons with one lost to aircraft). Notoro's damage was FLASHER's, off Borneo at about 0117 the same day (combinedfleet.com Notoro_t), not BANG's; Marifu Maru's was FLIER's on 13 June

translation: BANG fires all ten tubes at three ships at about 1510; Sarawak Maru is hit in the bow and Miri Maru under the bridge, and both reach Manila
note: Secondary. Time "about 1510" is BANG's (sheet 1508-1509 I); position is the source's. Temporary repairs at Cavite until 24 July

original: 〃 〇五一五 N一九-二二 E一一五-四三 栗 我雷撃ヲ受ク被害ナシ ?圧中
translation: (4th) 0515, N 19°22′ E 115°43′, from Kuri: we are under torpedo attack, no damage; (suppressing?)
note: 2nd China Expeditionary Fleet war diary, July 1944, enemy-submarine table (別図参照), read right to left; each position written vertically, N column then E column, in kanji numerals. Zone not stated; taken as I (Tokyo time), assumed. Kuri (栗) is a destroyer. The last word is unclear (列圧中 or 制圧中, 'suppressing', i.e. depth-charging). Nine minutes after BANG's Attack 3 (0506 I) and about 17 nm east-southeast of it; SEAHORSE logged depth charges eleven minutes after BANG fired

original: 四日東沙島南西海面ニ於テ第九一船団ハ二隻乃至三隻ト推定サル敵潜ノ執拗ナル攻撃ヲ受ケ護衛艦栗初雁ハ之ニ対シ適確ナル爆雷攻撃ヲ加ヘ重油流出ヲ認メタルモ効果ヲ確認シ得ズ
translation: On the 4th, in the waters southwest of Pratas Island, the No. 91 convoy came under persistent attack by enemy submarines estimated at two or three; the escorts Kuri and Hatsukari made accurate depth-charge attacks on them and saw oil come up, but could not confirm the result
note: 2nd China Expeditionary Fleet war diary, July 1944, narrative (一) 敵情, (ロ) 敵潜ノ動静. Names the convoy of J04 and of SEAHORSE patrol 5 J01-J02 (第九一船団). 乃至 read from a cramped hand. Two boats were there (SEAHORSE and BANG); the estimate of two or three is the diary's
